audit_findings.title: The owner-earnings anchor is stale and mixed with 2026 balance-sheet and share data
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; omitted FY2025 filed net income was $65.945 million, adjusted net income was $1,026.421 million, operating cash flow was $890.762 million, and capex was $469.838 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The omitted FY2025 results and available 2026 interim activity affect the OE anchor and growth assessment, while June 2026 cash, claims, debt and a 139.102212 million diluted-share denominator are already used in the bridge and per-share calculation.
audit_findings.evidence: Our discussion of our results focuses on 2024 and 2023 and year-to-year comparisons between those periods.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated dating error, not merely a possibility: the valuation identifies FY2024 as the latest actual even though a FY2025 10-K and June 2026 interim statements are supplied. FY2025 contained major pension, credit-loss, asbestos, restructuring and working-capital changes, and first-half 2026 added further operating results and financing changes. The proper current-period OE cannot be derived from the supplied valuation, so the direction and exact magnitude are unresolved, but replacing a $1,084.9 million anchor can reasonably change every scenario and the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct FY2025 OE from the filed 10-K, build a June 2026 trailing-twelve-month OE bridge with documented treatment of pension settlement, asbestos remeasurement, First Brands losses, restructuring, separation costs and the $250 million A/R-sale cash-flow benefit, then rerun all scenarios using bridge assets, claims and diluted shares from the same date.

audit_findings.title: FY2024 owner earnings may retain pension income that is known to disappear
audit_findings.magnitude: $54 million pretax; computed maximum direct bull-case effect of approximately $847 million or $6.09 per share if the entire pretax amount was retained in OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unpurged non-service pension income inflates the OE anchor and is capitalized through forecast and terminal value; pension-plan assets must also be excluded from the bridge unless distributable to common shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: The termination of our U.S. plan will significantly reduce pension income prospectively.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the $54 million was retained is unresolved because the anchor reconciliation is absent. Nevertheless, treating the entire pretax amount as an OE overstatement gives a conservative upper direct effect of about $6.09 per share using the bull operating-value-to-anchor multiple. That is smaller than the $7.90 gap between the $130.18 bull value and the $138.08 market price, and correction can only lower value. The filing also establishes that the $246 million June 2026 bond fund is designated for defined-contribution-plan funding rather than freely distributable cash.
audit_findings.action: Produce the FY2024 OE reconciliation proving whether the $54 million non-service pension income was removed and trace all pension-related assets out of unrestricted cash or stakes; rerun the anchor if either item was included.

audit_findings.title: The $527.3 million stakes addition is insufficiently defined and may include assets tied to offsetting claims
audit_findings.magnitude: $527.3 million bridge addition, equal to $3.79 per share; associated claims and any OE income double count are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The amount is added directly to equity value, while restricted assets, related liabilities and investment income already captured in OE would require removal or netting.
audit_findings.evidence: Other assets consist primarily of cash surrender value of life insurance policies, equity method and other investments, guarantee fees receivable, and deferred compensation benefits.
audit_findings.explanation: The lack of a component schedule is demonstrated, and the filing identifies mixed items rather than a homogeneous portfolio of distributable stakes. Eliminating the entire stated addition alone would reduce value by $3.79 per share, insufficient to close the $7.90 price-to-bull-value gap. Materiality remains unresolved, however, because the record does not quantify associated deferred-compensation, insurance, guarantee, tax or other senior claims, or any income that may have been capitalized in OE as well as represented in the bridge.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $527.3 million line by line to the June 2026 balance sheet; document ownership, liquidity, operating purpose, restrictions and related liabilities for each component; exclude the $246 million plan-designated bond fund unless legally distributable; verify the corresponding income purge; and rerun the bridge and OE for all unsupported components.

audit_findings.title: The asbestos liability may be an undeducted claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: computed June 2026 net accrued claim of $258 million ($294 million liability less $36 million insurance receivable), equal to $1.85 per share; filed net range $204 million to $336 million, equal to $1.47 to $2.42 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: An existing net asbestos obligation not already represented in OE or the bridge should reduce equity value, subject to avoiding duplication of recurring asbestos expense retained in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The amount accrued for pending and future claims was $ 256 million as of December 31, 2024, which represented our best estimate of the liability within our calculated range of $ 219 million to $ 313 million, discounted using a discount rate of 4.58 %.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the bridge already recognizes the claim is unresolved, but its current scale is filed. Even deducting the upper end of the June 2026 accrued range net of the insurance receivable would lower value by approximately $2.42 per share, well below the $7.90 gap between market price and bull value, and it cannot reverse the present conclusion because the correction is downward. Future adverse remeasurement beyond the filed range is a separate monitoring risk.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $294 million liability and $36 million insurance receivable through stakes_net and all bridge schedules, identify asbestos expense retained or normalized in OE, and deduct the June 2026 net economic claim once—without double counting—if it is absent.

audit_findings.title: A sale-leaseback gain may have been capitalized as recurring owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $43.049 million pretax; computed maximum direct bull-case effect of approximately $675 million or $4.85 per share if the entire pretax gain was retained in OE
audit_findings.mechanism: A retained sale gain raises the FY2024 OE anchor and therefore forecast and terminal value, while recurring rent from continued occupancy remains an operating expense.
audit_findings.evidence: Partially offsetting the increase were $43 million in real estate sale gains, primarily from sale-leaseback transactions to enhance our financial operational flexibility on properties we continue to use in our ongoing operations.
audit_findings.explanation: Retention in the anchor is unresolved because no OE reconciliation is supplied; the FY2024 cash-flow statement separately adds back the $43.049 million gain, so a cash-flow-based construction may already exclude it. Even assuming the entire pretax gain remained in OE, its computed bull-case effect is about $4.85 per share, smaller than the $7.90 market-price gap, and removal only lowers value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2024 OE to the filed cash-flow statement, demonstrate that the $43.049 million gain was excluded while rent and lease cash costs remained included, and rerun the anchor if the gain survived the calculation.

audit_findings.title: Guarantees create a contingent senior claim outside reported debt
audit_findings.magnitude: $504 million filed maximum exposure at June 2026, equal to $3.62 per share before collateral recovery; expected loss unquantified; $29 million of guarantee assets and liabilities already recognized
audit_findings.mechanism: A guarantee payment or inadequately reserved expected credit loss would create a cash claim ahead of common equity and require a bridge deduction to the extent not already recognized in liabilities or OE.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2024, the total borrowings of the independents subject to guarantee by us were approximately $ 575 million, a decrease from $ 954 million at December 31, 2023.
audit_findings.explanation: The guarantees exist, but no present valuation error or material expected loss is demonstrated. The June 2026 filing reports collateral intended to recover all or a substantial portion of payments, no material guaranteed borrower in financial difficulty, no significant historical losses, and an immaterial current expected-credit-loss reserve. The $504 million maximum is not an expected loss and should not be deducted wholesale; deterioration in borrower credit or collateral coverage is forward-looking.
audit_findings.action: Monitor guaranteed principal, borrower credit quality, collateral values, CECL reserves, recognized stand-ready liabilities and separation allocation each reporting period; rerun the bridge only for a probability-weighted loss not already recognized in OE or liabilities.
